headline: 7 deaths from measles symptoms in 24 hours, 5 in Dhaka
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in measles cases and fatalities across Bangladesh.
details: Seven people with measles symptoms died within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday morning, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the seven fatalities recorded in the last 24 hours, five occurred in Dhaka district.
Since March 15 of this year, 170,638 people have been identified as suspected measles patients across the country.
Out of these suspected cases, 20,068 have been confirmed as measles infections.
During this period, 150,202 patients were admitted to hospitals, while 144,885 have been discharged after recovering.
The total number of deaths linked to measles and measles symptoms since March 15 has reached 1,019.
This marks a significant increase compared to previous years; in 2025, there were 132 cases, and in 2024, 247 cases were reported.
In 2023, 282 cases were recorded, and in 2022, 311 cases were reported, with no deaths recorded in those years.
caption:
7 deaths in 24 hours. A measles surge is hitting Bangladesh, with Dhaka being the hardest hit.

Seven people with measles symptoms died within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday morning, according to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Of the seven fatalities recorded in the last 24 hours, five occurred in Dhaka district.

Since March 15 of this year, 170,638 people have been identified as suspected measles patients across the country.

Out of these suspected cases, 20,068 have been confirmed as measles infections.

During this period, 150,202 patients were admitted to hospitals, while 144,885 have been discharged after recovering.

The total number of deaths linked to measles and measles symptoms since March 15 has reached 1,019.

This marks a significant increase compared to previous years; in 2025, there were 132 cases, and in 2024, 247 cases were reported.

In 2023, 282 cases were recorded, and in 2022, 311 cases were reported, with no deaths recorded in those years.
